page: Microsoft Azure FX2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 42.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 21.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 118 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates, such as 34.59 GB/sec in gzip and 14.46 GB/sec in bzip3. However, due to the low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the poor and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with uncached large block read bandwidth measured at a weak 21.69 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX2mds_v2 offers a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes high memory capacity and single-core speed over parallel processing power. This makes it a qualitative choice for workloads that require substantial memory footprints but do not scale across many threads. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, single-threaded data processing, lightweight database operations, and caching layers where high RAM-to-vCPU ratios are required without the overhead of paying for unneeded CPU cores.
